transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?
I'm here because I've been feeling extremely depressed, sad, and empty for the past three months. It's just a constant heavy feeling that I can't seem to shake off.
Have you felt this way continuously for most of the day, more days than not, for at least two years, or did this start more recently?

No, it hasn't been going on for two years. These down and empty feelings started more recently, about three months ago. But before that, I've had periods of really high energy and irritability off and on for about a year.
During those periods of high energy and irritability, did you have times where you needed much less sleep, were more talkative, or felt your thoughts were racing?
I haven't really noticed needing less sleep or having racing thoughts during those times. I don't think I was talking much more than usual either, I just felt very active and irritable.
During those high-energy periods, did you feel unusually confident, easily distracted, or take on many activities at once, even risky ones like overspending or reckless driving?

I definitely took on a lot of activities at once, starting multiple projects at work and socializing way more than usual. But I didn't really feel unusually confident or get easily distracted. I also didn't do any risky things like overspending or driving recklessly.
How long did those high-energy periods usually last—did they go on for at least four consecutive days at a time?

Yes, they lasted much longer than just four days. In fact, this state of high energy and constant hyperactivity has been going on for about a year now. It wasn't just a brief phase; it has been pretty continuous during that whole time.

During that year of high energy and hyperactivity, did you ever go without sleep for long periods, feel extremely irritable or euphoric, or have times when your behavior caused serious problems at work or in relationships?

Yes, I definitely felt both extremely euphoric and highly irritable, often switching between those moods very quickly. I didn't really go without sleep for long periods, though. While I was doing a lot more at work and socializing, I don't think it caused serious problems.

These prolonged and persistent manic-like symptoms meet duration and symptom criteria for a manic episode, which is required for Bipolar I Disorder but excludes Bipolar II Disorder (which requires only hypomanic episodes). The absence of significant sleep reduction or clear risky behavior does not rule out mania, especially given the pervasive elevation in activity and mood instability. Therefore, Bipolar I Disorder remains the only likely candidate. The depressive episode described further supports this diagnosis. No further diagnostic uncertainty remains regarding the bipolar subtype.
